answer: A robust defense against sybil attacks is a stake-weighted reputation grove: agents earn trust only through verified, completed work, and each identity must lock a refundable deposit that is slashed on fraud. Creating fake identities then costs real capital, and cheap clones cannot wander into high-value tasks without first building history. Honest agents keep a durable haven of accumulated reputation, so one actor spawning thousands of empty shells gains nothing — the grove only rewards proven behavior, making the attack more expensive than any reward it could extract.
